Modibo Keita: Who was the man?

Malian politician born in Bamako (1915-1977). A graduate of the William Ponty teacher-training college in Dakar in 1936, the following year he founded the Teachers' Union of French West Africa (AOF), with the Burkinabe Ouezzin Coulibaly. In 1946, he joined Felix Houphouet-Boigny to create, in Bamako, the African Democratic Rally (RDA).

Integrated into the inner circle of the representatives of the French Union in the National Assembly, he entered the cabinets of Bourges-Maunoury and of Felix Gaillard (1957). He is a federalist like most of the politicians of the savannah who dream of the unity of former times, but he is also pragmatic, because French Sudan is a landlocked country whose only lung is the railway that links it to the port of Dakar.

In 1959, he presided over the Mali Federation, which united his country with Senegal, but his personality and his friendship with Sekou Toure, who had left the French Community with a bang, clashed with the finely shaded socialist-leaning options of Leopold Senghor. After the break-up of the Federation, he continued to preside over his country, which had kept the prestigious name of Mali. Without breaking completely with France, he drew closer to Guinea and Ghana (creation of the Union of West African States), opted for "non-alignment", a formula of which he is the author, and took Mali out of the franc zone.

Financial difficulties and the growing scarcity of imported products, while an overstaffed administration absorbed most of the State budget, triggered muted opposition from the population. Public opinion turned when he created a militia that soon fell into corruption. The army, made up of officers trained in the French school, took advantage of this to seize power under the leadership of Lieutenant Moussa Traore (1968). Detained for long years in Kidal, the first president of the Malian Republic died on 16 May 1977.

Air Mali

Within the framework of the fundamental option of the party and the government, on 22 September 1960 the economic resolution called, among other things: for an immediate and rigorous attack on economic decolonisation; for the rapid establishment of new economic structures by overturning and developing commercial circuits within the framework of socialist planning founded on African realities; for the use of every means to put in place a rail, road, river and air infrastructure in keeping with the country's needs. It was therefore in application of these decisions that the national company Air Mali was created.

The operation of the domestic air network was carried out by the Air France company within the general framework of its inter-African operations and therefore did not supply the territory in depth. Three times a week, long-haul aircraft of the Air France-TAL-UAT company linked Bamako to France. Only three stopovers were served twice a week, two other stopovers once a week and two every fortnight (Nioro-Nara).

From October 1960 to December, activities focused above all on making contacts, shaping the company and recruiting the indispensable staff. It was in April 1961, following the receipt of three DC-3s, that Air Mali's role as an air carrier was to begin. Domestic routes: Segou, Mopti, Goundam, Timbuktu, Gao, Nara, Niafunke, Kayes, Nioro, Niono. If one considers the youth of this company at the time, we can affirm that it may deserve all the confidence that can be placed in it.

The development of tourism in the Republic of Mali will be a factor in the progress of air transport, given the conveniences it offers (speed, stability, safety, comfort). A continental country, Mali with its extensive surface area is obliged to rely on a solid airline to cope with rapid and coherent economic development.

Definitive transfers: Extract from the book of Colonel Assimi Souleymane Dembele, born in 1935 in Mouroudiah (Nara)

The book of Colonel Assimi Souleymane Dembele is terrible and edifying. Terrible because it shows an image of Mali that few people suspect. The memory of a land of great empires, a proud and peaceful people, a culture of insolent richness indeed characterise this country, a haven of peace in the quicksands that Africa has become. There is certainly that Mali, but there is another, more secret, less glorious one, that of the bullying, the torture, the assassinations that nobody talks about.

From the "socialist" era of Modibo Keita to the long reign of the military under the rule of Moussa Traore, these were thirty years of unspeakable violence. No one was spared, neither women, nor children, nor old people. As if governed by an implacable law, the chain of assassinations was unbroken, the executioners unfailingly ending up becoming the victims. And this, in the name of ideology, in the name of power. Mali was a relatively stable country under Modibo Keita as under Moussa Traore, but it is on reading Colonel Dembele's book that one understands the price the country paid for that stability: a life made of silence.

Silence of those who suffered the worst tortures, silence of their relatives, silence of the cadres, silence of the politicians. One day this question will have to be answered: how did a people that was nevertheless great endure such dictatorships for decades without flinching? The answer: In Mali, we went from single-partyism to multi-single-partyism. That means that we went from a single-party system to a system with a multitude of parties that still retain the reflexes of the single party. We chased away what comes naturally, and it came galloping back. Whereas 26 March 1991, a historic date for Malians, marks the end of the privileges of a dictatorship and of a regime built on the single party, nepotism and corruption.

How did a people that was nevertheless great sink? The answer to this question lies in an extraordinary fact in Mali: the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP) that struck our country under the single party of Moussa Traore and under democracy. The World Bank and USAID and other financial partners imposed and financed, within the framework of structural adjustment, liquidations of State companies and enterprises that brought about voluntary retirements. Several enterprises were liquidated: Editions et imprimeries du Mali (EDIM-SA), Societe Nationale d'Entreprise de Travaux Publics (SONETRA), Societe malienne d'import-export (SOMIEX), Societe malienne de conserves (SOMACO), Office des produits agricoles du Mali (OPAM), Societe des conserves du Mali (SOCOMA), Societe nationale de recherches et d'exploitation des ressources Minieres (SONAREM), Societe malienne des produits chimiques (SMPC), Societe nationale Air-Mali (AM), Regie des chemins de fer du Mali (CFM), Industrie textile du Mali (ITEMA), Usine de Bois, Librairie populaire du Mali, Societe nationale des hotelleries du Mali, Office malien du betail et de la viande (OMBEVI), Societe malienne du betail et des peaux (SOMBEPEC), Societe d'exploitation des produits oleagineux du Mali (SEPOM), Societe de construction radioelectrique du Mali (SOCORAM), Societe nationale de tabac et allumette du Mali (SONATAM), Union nationale des cooperatives (UNICOOP), Compagnie malienne de navigation (CMN), COMATEX, Societe des ciments du Mali (SOCIMA) at Diamou, Societe des tanneries maliennes (TAMALI), Mali Lait, etc.

In all, 5,666 civil servants were victims of the SAPs. More than a third of the civil servants of the public service were laid off between 1987 and 1993. The programme involved two (02) waves. The first 1987-1988 and 1989. The second wave: 1991-1992 and 1993. Since those years, the Structural Adjustment Programmes have created a social malaise. A social injustice, the source of all our ills.

Democracy was supposed to repair the wound; it inflamed it by redeploying its militants who were victims of the Structural Adjustment Programme into newly created institutions and services. From then on, gratuitous nastiness, jealousy and hatred entered our customs. The World Bank, USAID and the financial partners paid out 310 billion CFA francs to pay the entitlements of the laid-off workers.

Mali: grandeur and decadence of Modibo Keita

A country of high historical tradition, Mali corresponds to the former Sudan. It is a Muslim country in which part of the caste system that divides the population according to social functions survives. The dominant party is the Sudanese Union, an anti-colonialist revolutionary party led by Modibo Keita. It is relayed by local committees and youth movements, and at the 1959 elections it swept aside its rivals. After the failure of the Federation, Mali found itself alone, without access to the sea, dependent on France for 80% of its imports and obliged to send its products in transit through Burkina Faso and Cote d'Ivoire.

The government drew closer to Sekou Toure's Guinea and launched a campaign of nationalisations and collectivisation. A State company, the Societe malienne d'import-export (SOMIEX), was put in charge of exporting groundnuts, Mali's main source of income, and of importing everyday products.

Books and newspapers, banking, transport and pharmacy were also regulated at national level. Although Mali did not want to break with France, dissensions grew sharper with the former coloniser. The French military bases were evacuated, a Malian franc was created, which France refused to guarantee, the trade balance remained in deficit and operating expenditure increased, driven by civil-servant pay rises, administrative costs and the building of unproductive luxury facilities.

By 1967, the evidence had to be faced. The five-year plan had failed. In foreign policy, Mali supported the struggles waged in Algeria, in Congo Kinshasa and in Angola against imperialism. It tried to secure support in the East from China and the USSR, as in the West from the United States and Germany, through a policy of moderation that did not exclude firmness.

In domestic politics, Modibo Keita cultivated his trademark image of a wise man, obtained the Lenin Peace Prize and involved himself in the implementation of socialism. But this clashed with the individualism of the peasants. His puritanical policy (restriction of festivities, ban on games of chance) also displeased young people, who preferred parties to political talks. The Tuareg nomadic populations of the north entered into rebellion, demonstrations against forced austerity broke out in July 1962 and were brutally repressed.

Opposition leaders died in mysterious circumstances. At the 1964 elections, the single list of the Sudanese Union obtained 99.8% of the votes. But the country's finances did not recover, fraud picked up again more than ever, encouraged by corruption at State level, traders waged a creeping war against the authorities, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) refused a loan, France turned a deaf ear. Groundnut production collapsed. Modibo Keita replaced the party's political bureau with a National Committee for the Defence of the Revolution (CNDR), backed by people's militias. He believed he could count on France, with which he had just signed an agreement, when he was overthrown in November 1968 by Lieutenant Moussa Traore, who became head of State. This coup surprised international observers all the more in that it was not accompanied by any reaction from the population.

On the contrary, women and young people applauded the fall of socialism. But the honeymoon between the people and its leaders did not last. The regime gave in to corruption, waged war against its Burkinabe neighbour, grew poorer and, having distanced itself from the Eastern bloc countries, asked for the help of France, which intervened in 1984 to have it rejoin the Union. The Malian franc, devalued by half, returned to the franc zone. Moussa Traore was driven from power by an insurrection in March 1991.

In Mali, as in most West African countries, society is strongly hierarchical. It comprises two (02) large groups: the horons and the slaves. It belongs to the horons "tlobile" to lead our Mali, the griots teach us in their Tarik.

To better understand the upheavals, read these messages from two conservatives and traditionalists: "Pretentious peoples and youth, a day will come when this country will have as supreme chiefs only people of servile condition (slaves) to govern you."

The second adds: "If there are fifty-two (52) weeks in the year, it is not certain that the true noble families reach that number in Mali." Have we reached that stage? Surely yes.

GEOPOLITICS

The Mali of Modibo Keita and its achievements

Malian territory is situated in the zone of the central basins of West Africa. It is bounded to the north by the Algerian Sahara, to the north-east by Niger, to the east by Burkina Faso, to the south by Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea, to the west by Mauritania. In Mali is found the upper part of the Senegal River as well as 1,600 km of the Niger River, out of the 4,200 km of its course.

Political organisation

The Republic of Mali has been independent since 20 August 1960, the date of the break-up of the Mali Federation (Sudan-Senegal) whose independence had been proclaimed on 20 June 1960, but it would be officially proclaimed on 22 September 1960 by the National Assembly. The capital is Bamako. The Constitution, of the presidential type, was adopted by the National Assembly on 22 September 1960.

Executive power belongs to the president of the government, head of State. He is assisted in his decisions by the Political Bureau of the party of the Sudanese Union-African Democratic Rally (US-RDA). The president at the time was Modibo Keita. Legislative power belongs to the Assembly elected by direct universal suffrage for five (05) years. It comprised 80 deputies. The Sudanese Union-RDA (African Democratic Rally) party was a single party.

The General Union of Workers of Mali (UGTM) brought together all unionised workers. All the influential members of the union were members of the party's Political Bureau.

Mali was a member:
- of the Casablanca group (headquarters of the permanent bureau in Bamako),
- of the franc zone (subject to the remarks made in chapter VIII),
- of the West African customs union,
- of the UN (27 September 1960) and of the major international organisations, including the IMF since 1963,
Of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU). Mali was, in addition, associated with the Common Market.

The State: On the threshold of independence, Mali attempted a Federation with Senegal which ended in failure (20 August 1960). The Republic of Mali was then proclaimed, on 22 September 1960 of the same year, indivisible, democratic, secular and social: "One People, One Goal, One Faith". The president of the government is invested by the National Assembly by absolute majority. He is head of State and guardian of the Constitution. He appoints the ministers and the ambassadors, signs and ratifies treaties. He is the supreme head of the Armed Forces.

The Administration: Mali was divided into six (06) administrative regions whose governors were appointed; and who were assisted by regional assemblies elected by universal suffrage. Subdivisions: cercles (appointed commanders + cercle councils); arrondissements (arrondissement councils); communes (elected mayors + village councils). The six (06) regions totalled forty-two (42) cercles and one hundred and thirty (230) arrondissements. The tribes and nomadic fractions of the North were led by elected tribal councils.

Public Health: Two (02) first-category hospitals (Bamako). Six (06) secondary hospitals (Gao, Markala, Mopti, Segou, Sikasso, Kayes). The whole of the health infrastructure developed considerably (thirty-nine (39) hospital centres, two hundred and fifty (250) dispensaries, seven (07) leprosaria, forty-seven (45) maternity units, mother-and-child protection centres, infirmaries, a blood bank, screening and radiography trucks). One cannot mention this infrastructure without referring to the Marchoux Institute (leprosy) and the IOTA (African Institute of Tropical Ophthalmology), a research centre concerning tropical ophthalmology.

Justice: the customary courts were abolished. The judicial organisation comprised the following levels: High Court of Justice (composed of elected deputies), competent where appropriate to try ministers, even the head of State; the State Court (three sections: constitution, litigation, accounts), called upon to settle disputes at governmental level; Assize Court, Court of Appeal, courts of first instance, justices of the peace, labour courts.

Diplomacy: Mali had some twenty diplomatic representatives abroad, notably in the United States, in Great Britain, in France, in the USSR and in the People's Republic of China. Nearly forty (40) countries were represented in Bamako. On the international level, our country was a member of numerous organisations, starting with the United Nations and the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), the International Labour Organization (ILO), the World Health Organization (WHO), etc.

The Armed Forces: The strength of the Armed Forces was around 3,000 men. There was a military school for the training of officers. The equipment (tanks, aircraft) was of Soviet origin. The army took part in the life of the nation (administration of certain regions, cultivation of collective fields, literacy teaching).

Finances: In 1962, our country left the franc zone and created its own currency: the Malian franc, equivalent to the CFA franc. On 17 January 1967, talks began with France to reintegrate Mali into the franc zone (agreement signed 15 February 1967).

In May of the same year, the Malian franc was devalued by 50%. Its new value is defined by an equivalent in gold (0.0018 grams of fine gold). The issuing institution was the BRM (Bank of the Republic of Mali).

Investments: Three (03) sectors shared the range of investments:
- a Malian and foreign private sector, representing more than ten thousand (10,000) trading licences;
- a cooperative and mutualist sector whose development is constantly increasing;
- a public-interest sector reserved for the State and within which a certain number of activities are oriented according to the objectives of the plan.

Agriculture: Local production is, in Mali, the base of the economy. It is therefore to the peasantry that the socialist planning of the country applied first and foremost. The cooperative form is the essential structure of this economy. All the mutual societies are affiliated to a Territorial Fund for Economic Action. The Institute of Rural Economy (IER) draws up the agricultural development programmes, in correlation with the Plan.

Finally, Rural Expansion Centres deal with the drilling of wells, land development and the cropping calendar. The millet-sorghum group is Mali's leading production (1,200,000 hectares). Average annual production: 800,000 tonnes. However, rice cultivation is being intensified because it is considered to be of greater nutritional value for the population.

Industry: The industries deriving from agricultural production are the most important (rice mills, cotton ginning, kapok defibring, food preserves and beverages). Livestock production has led to the installation of refrigerated slaughterhouses in Gao and Bamako.

Flour mills and tanneries complete this industrialisation of livestock and agricultural products. Other manufacturing industries: cement works, brickworks, textile complex, electronic equipment, ceramics, paper mill, matches, cigarettes.

Mines: The most important operation that was in activity was that of the rock-salt quarries of Taoudenit (3,500 tonnes per year). But important metal deposits exist in Mali. The Plan provided for their exploitation as and when prospecting proved positive. The Mining Bureau was created with a view to promoting the research, exploitation and transformation of the riches of the subsoil. The "prospective" covers gold, platinum, uranium, thorium, lithium, bauxite, phosphates, copper, iron, manganese, etc. Marble quarries are already being worked. Oil drilling has been undertaken, notably to the north-east of Gao.

Fishing: This is one of Mali's very real riches (50,000 tonnes of fresh fish). The main fishing regions: Mopti: 25,000 tonnes. Segou: 15,000 tonnes. Gao: 8,500 tonnes. Dried fish is, along with groundnuts, cotton and livestock, an important department of exports.

Major facilities. Dams: three in number. Electricity: installed capacity: 15,425 kW. Seven (07) power stations.

Roads: around 12,000 km (national: 5,600 km; regional: 1,660 km; local: 4,820 km). Two thirds of the road network is passable in all seasons.

The river network: 1,750 km navigable on the Niger during certain times of the year. The Senegal is navigable from Kayes, in the far west of the country.

Airports: Bamako airport, class B, is usable for long-haul aircraft: DC7s, jets and Ilyushin 18s. The Air-Mali company operated weekly services to France, Morocco and the main African capitals. Other airports: Segou, Goundam, Gao, Timbuktu, Kayes, Nioro.

The railways: The whole Malian portion of the Dakar-Niger (or Niger-Ocean) line, extended beyond Bamako as far as Koulikoro. In all 645 km.

The Population: Four fifths of the population lives in the western part, one tenth in the towns. In the north, the population is nomadic or semi-nomadic. Average population density: 3.7 per square kilometre. Towns: the capital, Bamako (150,000 inhabitants). The other main towns were: Kayes, Sikasso, Segou, Mopti, Gao, Timbuktu.

Races and religions: No fewer than twenty-three (23) different ethnic groups are counted, whose names, for some of them at least, have some renown: Bambara, Fulani, Tuareg, Toucouleur, Dogon. Nearly one and a half million inhabitants were animists. Just as numerous are the Muslims. About thirty thousand were Christians.

Languages: Numerous languages or dialects, specifically Mandingo (two thirds of the population). Arabic is also spoken. French is the official language.

Means of expression: Radio.
A State body, Radio-Mali possessed about ten transmitters. Radio-Mali broadcast in French, in English, and in several regional languages, Bambara, Fulani, etc. Numerous collective-listening receivers existed in public places and schools.

Press: "L'Essor": daily and weekly edition. It is the organ of the Sudanese Union. Daily bulletin of the National Information Agency of Mali (ANIM). Monthly bulletins of the Tourism Plan. Liaison bulletin of the Office du Niger (Segou).

Employment: The number of wage earners was around 18,800, that is a very low percentage of the active population, the latter being estimated at 2,300,000 individuals. The distribution of wages by sector shows that 32% of them were paid in the public sector, 19% in trade and banking, 15% in building and public works, 11% in agriculture, 10% in transport, 9% in industry, the rest being distributed between the liberal professions and domestic service. Because of the three factors mentioned - strong demographic pressure, a young population, rapid growth of the towns - a problem of underemployment arises in Mali, particularly in urban centres.

Education: In Mali, the question of teaching was marked immediately after independence by a wide-ranging reform: the primary-secondary divide was abolished by the creation of the fundamental school grouping the former primary school and the first cycle of secondary. A large place was reserved, in addition, for practical work. 16% of the budget was devoted to education. The school attendance rate rose from 8 to 11.5%. Fundamental cycle: 700 schools. Secondary and technical cycle: sixteen (16) schools. Higher education: National School of Administration (ENA); School of Medicine. Numerous students abroad (Africa, Europe, the former USSR). There were several scientific research centres: fundamental, medical, agronomic.

In 1960, the school enrolment rate (UNESCO calculation) was still very low: 10%, and illiteracy reached 95% of the total population. In the same year, Mali had on average forty-one (41) teachers per 100,000 inhabitants. A very particular effort was therefore undertaken in this field and for 1963, the number of pupils in primary education was up by 80% compared with 1962.

The Plan also provided for the construction of a new lycee with a capacity of 1,200 pupils, of whom 900 boarders. In parallel, the reform of the curricula was to allow better adapted teaching. The National School of Administration of Mali provided the training of senior managers and high-ranking civil servants.

Source: Documents assembled by the Editorial Staff

a4045.t:
Africa CDC and WHO have updated their joint Continental Response Plan for the mpox emergency as the disease continues to affect new areas. The revised strategy focuses on controlling outbreaks, while expanding vaccination coverage and transitioning toward a longer-term, sustainable response.
Mpox is a viral illness that spreads between people, mainly through close contact. It causes painful skin and mucosal lesions, often accompanied by fever, headache, muscle aches, back pain, fatigue, and swollen lymph nodes. The disease can be debilitating and disfiguring.
Historically a zoonotic disease transmitted from infected animals, mpox has increasingly shown a tendency to spread between people. In 2022, a variant of the virus, clade IIb, began spreading globally through sexual contact. Since late 2023, yet another viral strain, clade Ib, began spreading through sexual networks and within households and through close contact. This prompted Africa CDC to declare a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security and the WHO Director-General to declare a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in August 2024.
By August 2024, the virus had begun spreading from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to 4 neighbouring countries. Since then, 28 countries around the world have reported cases of mpox due to clade Ib. Outside Africa, cases remain largely travel-related. However, within Africa, in addition to transmission in Burundi, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda, local transmission has now been documented in additional countries including the Republic of the Congo, South Africa, South Sudan, the United Republic of Tanzania and Zambia.
Since the declaration of the emergency, both regional and global support has increased, particularly for the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the epicentre of the outbreak. The Africa CDC and WHO Joint Continental Mpox Plan has guided these efforts, focusing on ten key pillars: coordination, risk communication and community engagement, disease surveillance, laboratory capacity, clinical management, infection prevention and control, vaccination, research, logistics, and maintaining essential health services.
Vaccination efforts are underway, with more than 650 000 doses administered in 6 countries, 90% of which have been administered in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Overall, over a million doses have been delivered to 10 countries, with efforts ongoing to secure additional vaccine supplies.
Diagnostic testing capacity in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has grown significantly, driven by the expansion of laboratory infrastructure – from 2 laboratories in late 2023 to 23 laboratories in 12 provinces today. With new, near-point-of-care tests currently being rolled out in the country, capacity is expected to increase even further.
Despite this progress, major challenges remain. Ongoing conflict and insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the incidence of mpox remains high, as well as humanitarian aid cuts, continue to limit the public health response and restrict access to essential services. Across countries and partners, over US$ 220 million is needed to fill funding gaps for the mpox response.
The updated Continental Response Plan calls for intensified efforts to bring outbreaks under control, while also taking concrete actions to integrate mpox into routine health services.
Along with the Continental Response Plan for Africa, WHO has updated the global strategic plan to curb – and where feasible, to stop – human-to-human transmission of mpox. In the first two months of 2025, 60 countries reported mpox, with the majority of cases and deaths reported from the African continent. The joint Continental Response Plan is aligned with the global strategy.
Africa CDC and WHO continue to work closely with national governments, local communities, and partners to curb transmission, control the outbreak, and build longer-term resilience within public health systems.

a4131.t:
Simon Shuster est le correspondant principal de Time pour l’Ukraine et la Russie.
Pour avoir écrit des articles élogieux sur l'(ancien) président Zelensky, Shuster a bénéficié d’un accès extraordinaire au bureau du président ukrainien. Un portrait ultérieur de Shuster dépeint Zelensky comme délirant. Dans son dernier article, il affirme que l’administration Biden n’a jamais eu l’intention de faire gagner l’Ukraine :
«Lorsque la Russie a envahi l’Ukraine il y a près de trois ans, le président Joe Biden a fixé trois objectifs à la réponse américaine. La victoire de l’Ukraine n’en a jamais fait partie».
L’un des trois objectifs de Joe Biden était d’empêcher une guerre entre la Russie et l’OTAN, et non la victoire de l’Ukraine.
C’est pourquoi, tout au long de la guerre en Ukraine, les États-Unis, de concert avec l’Allemagne, ont bloqué l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN.
En septembre, la dernière tentative de Zelensky auprès de Biden pour obtenir l’accès à l’OTAN s’est terminée sans succès :
«Les appels [de Zelensky] ont reçu un accueil mitigé. Sur la question de l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN, Biden n’a pas voulu bouger».
Il en a toujours été ainsi et il en sera toujours ainsi.
Bien qu’elle ait été rejetée à maintes reprises, Zelensky a utilisé l’espoir d’obtenir l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN (et à l’UE) pour commercialiser la guerre qu’il menait.
Aujourd’hui, alors qu’il est manifestement en train de la perdre, il reproche à ceux qui ne lui ont jamais promis l’adhésion à l’OTAN de ne pas l’avoir obtenue :
«Les promesses de l’Occident d’accepter un jour l’Ukraine dans l’OTAN étaient un «mensonge». C’est ce qu’a affirmé le président Volodymyr Zelensky lors du Forum économique mondial de Davos.
De plus, selon lui, les États-Unis et l’Allemagne ont maintenu des contacts avec la Russie tout au long de la guerre.
«De la part de certains États, je pense qu’au départ ce n’était pas une politique très transparente, ils ne nous soutenaient pas dans l’OTAN. Ils ne nous ont pas soutenus dans l’OTAN et se sont contentés de dire que l’Ukraine ferait partie de l’OTAN. Ce n’était pas juste pour l’Ukraine et les Ukrainiens. Et ce n’était pas juste non plus de la part de nos dirigeants. Lorsque certains de nos dirigeants ont dit et promis que nous serions dans l’OTAN, ce n’était pas juste non plus. Ce n’était pas juste non plus. Je pense que l’Allemagne et les États-Unis ont adopté une position de faiblesse. Parce qu’ils avaient un dialogue avec les Russes. Et je crois qu’ils ont perdu ce dialogue. Nous avons perdu, parce qu’ils font toujours appel au fait qu’il y a eu des accords avec les Russes», a déclaré Zelensky».
Cette fausse accusation à l’encontre des pays étrangers, qui promettent l’accès à l’OTAN mais ne le donnent pas, ne sera pas bien accueillie.
Comme le remarque Strana :
«Rappelons que Zelensky lui-même a affirmé à plusieurs reprises que l’Ukraine ferait partie de l’OTAN.
De plus, Kiev exige maintenant l’admission dans l’Alliance comme condition pour faire la paix avec la Russie. Dans le même temps, Zelensky admet que les États-Unis et l’Allemagne s’y opposent».
Alexey Arestovich, ancien conseiller de Zelensky, répond à son affirmation :
«– Que dites-vous ?
Qui est le principal responsable de la diffusion massive de ce mensonge auprès des Ukrainiens, de la persécution de ceux qui ont dit qu’il n’y aurait pas d’OTAN, que c’est une escroquerie, que nous sommes trompés, et que nous avons signé pour sacrifier nos vies pour cela, avez-vous la force de le nommer ?»
Ce à quoi le professeur Glenn Diesen ajoute :
«Les médias occidentaux sont également responsables : Toute personne s’opposant à la mise en place et au sacrifice des Ukrainiens dans le cadre d’une guerre par procuration a été traitée de propagandiste de la Russie. Seule une propagande de guerre infâme et implacable a été autorisée dans les médias».
La guerre par procuration menée par les États-Unis contre la Russie, qui a sacrifié l’Ukraine, était basée sur des recherches sur la manière de faire «s‘étendre la Russie» publiées en 2019 par le groupe de réflexion du Pentagone, la RAND Corp. Cette recherche a été initiée par trois questions :
«1. Quelles sont les plus grandes inquiétudes et vulnérabilités de la Russie ?
2. De quelle manière ces inquiétudes et ces vulnérabilités peuvent-elles être exploitées pour faire s’étendre la Russie ?
3. Quels sont les coûts et les risques associés à chaque option, et quelles sont les perspectives de succès ?»
La RAND a constaté que la manière la plus favorable de «faire s’étendre la Russie» était d’utiliser l’Ukraine dans une guerre contre elle en lui fournissant des armes létales :
«Les États-Unis pourraient accroître leur assistance militaire à l’Ukraine – en termes de quantité et de qualité des armes. (…)
Les États-Unis pourraient également soutenir plus vigoureusement l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN. Alors que l’exigence d’unanimité de l’OTAN rend improbable l’adhésion de l’Ukraine dans un avenir prévisible, le fait que Washington insiste sur cette possibilité pourrait renforcer la détermination de l’Ukraine tout en amenant la Russie à redoubler d’efforts pour empêcher une telle évolution».
Au moment où le conseil de la RAND a été publié, il avait déjà été suivi. Peu après le coup d’État du Maïdan en 2014, la CIA avait lancé une coopération intensive avec les services de renseignement militaires ukrainiens.
«Le partenariat a vu la CIA aider l’Ukraine à reconstruire sa Direction principale du renseignement, connue sous l’acronyme HUR, qui est devenue célèbre pour ses opérations audacieuses. La CIA a finalement consacré des millions de dollars à la formation et à l’équipement des agents de renseignement ukrainiens, ainsi qu’à la construction d’installations, notamment d’une douzaine de bases secrètes d’opérations avancées à la frontière avec la Russie. Les deux services ont également commencé à mener ensemble des opérations conjointes dans le monde entier, le plus haut niveau de confiance pour les services de renseignement, selon les anciens responsables américains».
En 2017, l’administration Trump a commencé à livrer ouvertement des missiles antichars Javelin à l’Ukraine. En 2021, lorsque Biden a pris le relais, les États-Unis ont continué à suivre le conseil de la RAND. Le flux d’armes létales vers l’Ukraine a augmenté. Un soutien verbal à l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’OTAN a été apporté par les médias et lors de réunions d’information anonymes. Mais cela n’a jamais été énoncé comme un objectif officiel, car les États-Unis savaient qu’il n’y avait aucun moyen d’y parvenir.
La RAND a énuméré les «avantages» que les États-Unis, et non l’Ukraine, tireraient probablement de cette adhésion. Mais ces avantages découlaient de l’affaiblissement de la Russie, et non de gains réels pour les États-Unis eux-mêmes.
Le rapport énumère également des risques :
«La Russie pourrait aussi provoquer une contre-escalade en engageant davantage de troupes et en les poussant plus profondément en Ukraine. La Russie pourrait même devancer l’action des États-Unis, en intensifiant la situation avant l’arrivée de toute aide américaine supplémentaire. Une telle escalade pourrait faire s’étendre la Russie ; l’est de l’Ukraine est déjà un gouffre. S’emparer d’une plus grande partie de l’Ukraine ne ferait qu’alourdir le fardeau, même si c’est aux dépens du peuple ukrainien. Toutefois, une telle initiative pourrait également avoir un coût important pour l’Ukraine ainsi que pour le prestige et la crédibilité des États-Unis. Elle pourrait entraîner un nombre disproportionné de victimes ukrainiennes, des pertes territoriales et des flux de réfugiés. Elle pourrait même conduire l’Ukraine à une paix désavantageuse».
Les risques décrits par la RAND sont désormais l’issue évidente de la guerre.
Tout cela était connu et disponible grâce à des sources facilement accessibles.
Il est difficile de comprendre pourquoi Zelensky, ou tout autre Ukrainien, s’attendait à autre chose.
L’une des explications est que Zelensky s’est vraiment fourvoyé comme Shuster l’a décrit :
«Sa croyance en la victoire finale de l’Ukraine sur la Russie s’est durcie et inquiète certains de ses conseillers. Elle est inébranlable, à la limite du messianisme. «Il se fait des illusions», me dit l’un de ses plus proches collaborateurs, frustré. «Nous n’avons plus d’options. Nous ne sommes pas en train de gagner. Mais essayez de lui dire cela»».
Résolument opposé à toute négociation de paix, Zelensky formule des exigences de plus en plus criardes.
Outre l’adhésion immédiate à l’OTAN, il réclame désormais une force de maintien de la paix qui n’existe pas :
«Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky, qui cherche à rencontrer le président américain Donald Trump, affirme qu’au moins 200 000 casques bleus européens seront nécessaires pour empêcher une nouvelle attaque russe après tout accord de cessez-le-feu. (…) «De tous les Européens ? Deux cent mille, c’est un minimum. C’est un minimum, sinon ce n’est rien», a déclaré Zelensky lorsqu’il a été interrogé sur l’idée d’un contingent de maintien de la paix dans le cadre d’une interview après avoir prononcé son discours.
Ce nombre correspond à peu près à la taille de l’ensemble des forces armées françaises, estimées à un peu plus de 200 000 par le ministère français de la Défense en 2020».
Il souhaite également que les forces américaines en fassent partie.
Il n’y a aucune chance d’obtenir l’un ou l’autre.
Zelensky est fini et il le sait. Il est peu probable qu’il soit encore en place dans trois mois environ.
source : https://reseauinternational.net/
a4131.en:
Simon Shuster is Time's senior correspondent for Ukraine and Russia.

For having written flattering articles about (former) President Zelensky, Shuster enjoyed extraordinary access to the Ukrainian president's office. A later portrait by Shuster depicts Zelensky as delusional. In his latest article he asserts that the Biden administration never intended to make Ukraine win:

"When Russia invaded Ukraine nearly three years ago, President Joe Biden set three objectives for the American response. Ukraine's victory was never one of them."

One of Joe Biden's three objectives was to prevent a war between Russia and NATO, not a Ukrainian victory.

That is why, throughout the war in Ukraine, the United States, together with Germany, blocked Ukraine's accession to NATO.

In September, Zelensky's latest attempt with Biden to obtain access to NATO ended without success:

"[Zelensky's] appeals met with a mixed reception. On the question of Ukraine's NATO membership, Biden would not budge."

It has always been this way and it will always be this way.

Although it was rejected time and again, Zelensky used the hope of obtaining Ukraine's membership in NATO (and the EU) to market the war he was waging.

Today, while he is manifestly losing it, he blames those who never promised him NATO membership for not having obtained it:

"Western promises to one day admit Ukraine into NATO were a 'lie'. That is what President Volodymyr Zelensky asserted at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

Moreover, according to him, the United States and Germany maintained contacts with Russia throughout the war.

'On the part of certain States, I think that at the outset it was not a very transparent policy, they did not support us in NATO. They did not support us in NATO and merely said that Ukraine would be part of NATO. That was not fair to Ukraine and Ukrainians. And it was not fair on the part of our leaders either. When some of our leaders said and promised that we would be in NATO, that was not fair either. That was not fair either. I think that Germany and the United States adopted a position of weakness. Because they had a dialogue with the Russians. And I believe they lost that dialogue. We lost, because they always appeal to the fact that there were agreements with the Russians,' Zelensky declared."

This false accusation against foreign countries, which promise access to NATO but do not give it, will not be well received.

As Strana notes:

"Let us recall that Zelensky himself asserted on several occasions that Ukraine would be part of NATO.

Moreover, Kyiv is now demanding admission to the Alliance as a condition for making peace with Russia. At the same time, Zelensky admits that the United States and Germany are opposed to it."

Alexey Arestovich, former adviser to Zelensky, responds to his assertion:

"- What are you saying?

Who is the main person responsible for the massive spread of this lie to Ukrainians, for the persecution of those who said that there would be no NATO, that it is a swindle, that we are being deceived, and that we signed up to sacrifice our lives for it — do you have the strength to name him?"

To which Professor Glenn Diesen adds:

"The Western media are also responsible: Anyone opposing the setting up and sacrifice of Ukrainians in the framework of a proxy war was called a propagandist for Russia. Only vile and relentless war propaganda was allowed in the media."

The proxy war waged by the United States against Russia, which sacrificed Ukraine, was based on research on how to make Russia "overextend" published in 2019 by the Pentagon think tank RAND Corp. This research was initiated by three questions:

"1. What are Russia's greatest anxieties and vulnerabilities?
2. In what ways can these anxieties and vulnerabilities be exploited to overextend Russia?
3. What are the costs and risks associated with each option, and what are the prospects for success?"

RAND found that the most favourable way to "overextend Russia" was to use Ukraine in a war against it by providing it with lethal weapons:

"The United States could increase its military assistance to Ukraine — in terms of the quantity and quality of weapons. (...)

The United States could also more vigorously support Ukraine's accession to NATO. While NATO's unanimity requirement makes Ukraine's membership unlikely in the foreseeable future, Washington's insistence on this possibility could strengthen Ukraine's resolve while leading Russia to redouble its efforts to prevent such a development."

By the time RAND's advice was published, it had already been followed. Shortly after the 2014 Maidan coup, the CIA had launched intensive cooperation with Ukrainian military intelligence.

"The partnership saw the CIA help Ukraine rebuild its Main Intelligence Directorate, known by the acronym HUR, which became famous for its daring operations. The CIA ultimately devoted millions of dollars to training and equipping Ukrainian intelligence officers, as well as to building facilities, notably a dozen secret forward operating bases on the border with Russia. The two services also began conducting joint operations together around the world, the highest level of trust for intelligence services, according to the former US officials."

In 2017, the Trump administration began openly delivering Javelin anti-tank missiles to Ukraine. In 2021, when Biden took over, the United States continued to follow RAND's advice. The flow of lethal weapons to Ukraine increased. Verbal support for Ukraine's accession to NATO was provided by the media and in anonymous briefings. But it was never stated as an official objective, because the United States knew there was no way to achieve it.

RAND listed the "advantages" that the United States, and not Ukraine, would likely derive from that membership. But those advantages flowed from the weakening of Russia, and not from real gains for the United States itself.

The report also lists risks:

"Russia could also provoke a counter-escalation by committing more troops and pushing them deeper into Ukraine. Russia could even pre-empt US action, escalating the situation before any additional American aid arrives. Such an escalation could overextend Russia; eastern Ukraine is already a money pit. Seizing a larger part of Ukraine would only add to the burden, even if it is at the expense of the Ukrainian people. However, such an initiative could also come at a significant cost to Ukraine as well as to the prestige and credibility of the United States. It could result in a disproportionate number of Ukrainian casualties, territorial losses and refugee flows. It could even lead Ukraine to a disadvantageous peace."

The risks described by RAND are now the obvious outcome of the war.

All of this was known and available through easily accessible sources.

It is difficult to understand why Zelensky, or any other Ukrainian, expected anything else.

One explanation is that Zelensky really did lose his way, as Shuster described:

"His belief in Ukraine's final victory over Russia has hardened and worries some of his advisers. It is unshakeable, bordering on messianism. 'He's deluding himself,' one of his closest aides tells me, frustrated. 'We have no more options. We are not winning. But try telling him that.'"

Resolutely opposed to any peace negotiation, Zelensky is formulating increasingly strident demands.

Besides immediate accession to NATO, he is now demanding a peacekeeping force that does not exist:

"Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who is seeking to meet American President Donald Trump, asserts that at least 200,000 European peacekeepers will be needed to prevent a new Russian attack after any ceasefire agreement. (...) 'Of all the Europeans? Two hundred thousand, that's a minimum. That's a minimum, otherwise it's nothing,' Zelensky said when asked about the idea of a peacekeeping contingent in an interview after delivering his speech.

That number corresponds roughly to the size of the entire French armed forces, estimated at a little over 200,000 by the French Defence Ministry in 2020."

He also wants American forces to be part of it.

There is no chance of obtaining either.

Zelensky is finished and he knows it. He is unlikely to still be in place in about three months.

source: https://reseauinternational.net/

a4216.t:
ABUJA – The Senate President, Senator Godswill Obong Akpabio, on Wednesday, summoned Directors General of National Intelligence Agency (NIA), Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA), Department of State Services (DSS), and the National Security Adviser (NSA) to brief senators on the alleged involvement of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in the sponsorship of Boko Haram terrorist group.
Akpabio was responding to a motion by Senator Ali Ndume over a report in the social media by an American Congress man, alleging the involvement of USAID in the sponsorship of Boko Haram.
“I am convening an emergency closed session with the National Security Adviser, Director-General of the National Intelligence Agency, Director-General of the Department of State Services, and Director-General of the Defence Intelligence Agency to provide an immediate briefing on the allegations surrounding USAID’s funding of Boko Haram in Nigeria.
We must get to the bottom of this matter, and I expect a thorough and transparent briefing from our national security leadership,” he said.
Akpabio said it’s only through thorough investigation that the truth can be established, adding that even if America has not taken an obligation, hook, line, and sink, Nigeria must also investigate to be sure.
“Because we won’t just keep quiet. If it is true that USAID has been funding Boko Haram in Nigeria. We have no business allowing them to have offices in Nigeria and before we can take decisive steps and also ask for recompense in particular, we must go deeper into the issue.
So it’s important that we get briefed by our intelligence community,” he said.
Earlier, Senator Ali Ndume while presenting the motion before the Senate noted that on Thursday, 13th February, 2025, the entire social media space was agog with trending video of a United States Republican Congressman, Scott Perry, representing Pennsylvania, alleging at the inaugural hearing of subcommittee on delivering on government efficiency, USAID has been funding terrorist organisations across the world, Boko Haram inclusive.
He said this allegation is coming on the heels of the Chief of Defence Staff, General Christopher Musa, raising an alarm that Boko Haram terrorist groups are being sponsored and trained by international organisations.
Ndume also noted that over the years, the modus operandi of Boko Haram in Nigeria has been a source of great concern and their source of funding and operations have been shrouded in mystery.
According to him, the devastation caused by Boko Haram in the North-East region and other parts of the country, which includes the bombing of UN building in Abuja, and of course, the bombing of the Police Force Headquarters here in Abuja, among other attacks, led to loss of lives of Nigerians in thousands, unwarranted destruction on properties, which occasioned unprecedented internal displacement across the country.
He also recalls that the Federal Government over the years tried to put measures in place to curtail the activities of terrorist groups in the country by expending huge resources, which seem not to have yielded much result as the nefarious activities of terrorists continued unabatedly.
Ndume said the monumental devastation caused by Boko Haram in this country should be a matter of concern, as it has dented the image of this country among the comity of nations and for allegations to begin to emerge at this point in time that some international organisations are behind this unwholesome act, there is the urgent need for steps to be taken by the Federal Government to unravel the mystery behind this whole episode.
Senator Abdul Ningi, who was also a co-sponsor of the motion by Senator Ali Ndume, said it’s almost impossible to do justice to the issues raised by this motion unless the top brass of the security sector are invited to brief the Senate.
“The Senate needs to be briefed, first and foremost, by the heads of various security agencies in a closed-door session. I also don’t want this in the media because beyond the media, beyond what I know, beyond what you know, we have intelligence organisation, that is funded by this government,” he said.

a4233.t:
The Trump administration on Monday welcomed a small group of white South Africans as refugees, saying they face discrimination and violence at home, which the country’s government strongly denies. The decision to admit the 49 people also has raised questions from refugee advocates about why the group should be admitted when the Trump administration has suspended efforts to resettle people who are fleeing war and persecution and have gone through years of vetting before coming to the United States.
The group from South Africa, including children holding small American flags, arrived at Dulles International Airport outside Washington on a private charter plane and was greeted by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau and Homeland Security Deputy Secretary Troy Edgar. “I want you all to know that you are really welcome here and that we respect what you have had to deal with these last few years,” Landau told the group in a hangar at the airport, many of them holding U.S. flags.
“We respect the long tradition of your people and what you have accomplished over the years.” President Donald Trump told reporters earlier Monday that he’s admitting them as refugees because of the “genocide that’s taking place.” He said that in post-apartheid South Africa, white farmers are “being killed” and he plans to address the issue with South African leadership next week.
That characterization is strongly denied by the South African government and has been disputed by experts in the country and even an Afrikaner group. South Africa’s government says the U.S. allegations that the white minority Afrikaners are being persecuted are “completely false,” the result of misinformation and an inaccurate view of its country.
It cited the fact that Afrikaners are among the richest and most successful people in the country and said they are among “the most economically privileged.” Afrikaners make up South Africa’s largest white group and were the leaders of the apartheid government, which brutally enforced racial segregation for nearly 50 years before ending it in 1994. While South Africa has been largely successful in reconciling its many races after apartheid ended, tensions between some Black political parties and some Afrikaner groups have remained. Trump has promoted the allegation that white farmers in South Africa are being killed on a large scale because of their race as far back as 2018 during his first term.
Conservative commentators have promoted the allegation about a genocide against white farmers in South Africa, and South African-born Trump ally Elon Musk has posted on social media that some politicians in the country are “actively promoting white genocide.”

a4463.t:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Mozambique received a shipment of Shelter and Non-Food Items (NFIs) donated by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), which will improve the living conditions of at least 10,000 households (HHs) in central and northern Mozambique. This support, consisting of Plastic Tarpaulins, Plastic Sheeting Rolls, and 5,000 Shelter Fixing Kits, will allow the most vulnerable displaced population to have basic supplies to start their recovery, thus contributing to income generation and self-reliance of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities.
The increased security incidents in northern Mozambique since 2017, and extreme weather events including floods, cyclones and droughts that occur regularly, have resulted in the displacement of more than 784,564 people in Mozambique, mostly in the central and northern region (DTM Baseline Round 15, February 2022). 1.5 million people are estimated to be in need of humanitarian assistance (Humanitarian Response Plan, 2022).
This USAID contribution will be added to the central repository of shelter and household supplies (Common Shelter and NFI Pipeline), increasing the capacity of response of humanitarian partners to deliver an efficient life-saving emergency to those who continue to flee areas of instability and areas affected by natural disasters. As the Shelter Cluster Lead Agency (CLA) in northern Mozambique since 2019, and with the generous support of its partners, IOM has been managing and upscaling the Common Pipeline to respond to the urgent shelter needs of the displaced population in northern Mozambique. In response to the Gombe Cyclone that hit Mozambique in March 2022, more than 2,200 families received support from USAID through the Common Pipeline.
USAID Mission Director, Helen Pataki said, “USAID is committed to protecting lives and livelihoods, and reducing the impact of disasters on vulnerable populations by helping households and communities in Mozambique. USAID is proud to work with IOM to provide these supplies to meet the needs of affected Mozambicans.”
In addition to this in-kind donation, an additional USAID grant of over $1 million is expected to reinforce the Common Pipeline with over 75,000 Shelter and NFI items that will serve more than 46,000 people. Since 2021, over 450,000 people have received ongoing humanitarian assistance from IOM with support from the United States government. USAID support contributes to humanitarian coordination as well as providing comprehensive direct and indirect assistance through a multisectoral response, as well as critical in-kind donations of immediate shelter and NFIs.
“IOM with the support of its partners aims to manage the effects of displacement by assisting the most vulnerable populations across Mozambique. This significant contribution from USAID will go a long way; it is greatly needed and appreciated and contributes to IOM’s aim to ensure aid is provided to help meet the urgent needs of those most affected by displacement”, said IOM Mozambique Chief of Mission, Dr. Laura Tomm-Bonde.
IOM’s work to provide and coordinate Shelter and NFI support as part of emergency capacity is closely aligned with Objective 7 – Address and reduce vulnerabilities in migration – and Objective 15 – Provide access to basic services for migrants – of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM). In 2022, IOM funding requirements amount to USD 79.3 million to continue and scale up its Humanitarian, Development and Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach in northern Mozambique, contributing to conditions in crisis contexts that are more suitable for development efforts (IOM Mozambique Roadmap for northern Mozambique). Following an HDPN approach, IOM seeks to reach sustainable solutions striving to contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) while implementing the GCM.

a4465.t:
Muktasari:
- Waziri Mkuu Kassim Majaliwa atoa mwelekeo wa Serikali kuhusu sera ya nje ya Marekani.
Dodoma. Baada ya Shirika la Marekani la Maendeleo ya Kimataifa (USAID) kutangaza kusitisha utoaji fedha, Serikali imesema inajiimarisha kuhakikisha inakuza uchumi kwa kutumia vyanzo vya fedha na mapato kujazia maeneo yaliyopungua.
USAID imetangaza kusitisha utoaji fedha mpya na usambazaji wa fedha chini ya makubaliano ya malengo ya Maendeleo (DOAGs) hadi uhakiki kwa programu za msaada wa nchi zinazofadhiliwa na USAID utakapokamilika ndani ya siku 85 kuanzia Januari 24, 2025.
Mchakato wa uhakiki unalenga kuhakikisha msaada wa nje unalingana na ajenda ya sera ya nje ya Rais Donald Trump.
Waziri Mkuu Kassim Majaliwa akijibu swali la papo kwa hapo bungeni leo Februari 6, 2025 amesema Serikali inajiimarisha kukuza uchumi kwa kutumia rasilimali zilizopo ili kumudu utekelezaji katika maeneo yote muhimu yakiwamo ya sekta ya afya, elimu na maji.
Majaliwa amesema hayo akijibu swali la Mbunge wa Mbozi, George Mwanisongole aliyehoji Serikali inajipangaje kukabiliana na mabadiliko ya sera za nje za Marekani ambazo zinakwenda kuathiri utekelezaji wa sera za Tanzania kwenye maeneo kadhaa yakiwamo ya elimu na afya.
“Serikali inajipanga vipi na sera za mabadiliko ya nchi ya Marekani ambazo tangu Rais Donald Trump aingie madarakani amefanya mabadiliko makubwa ya sera ya nje ya nchi yake ambayo yanakwenda kuathiri utekelezaji wa sera zetu kwenye elimu, afya na kiuchumi,” amehoji.
Mbunge huyo ameitaja miradi hiyo kuwa ni inayofadhiliwa na USAID, Mradi wa Programu ya Kutekeleza Elimu kwa Matokeo (EP4R) na Programu ya kupunguza makali ya Virusi vya Ukimwi (VVU).
Majaliwa amesema Tanzania inaheshimu sera za mambo ya nje na inatekeleza mikataba ya sera hizo kama ambavyo wamekubaliana na nchi husika kwenye maeneo mbalimbali.
“Tumeanza kuona nchi zenye uwezo mkubwa ikiwemo Marekani na mabadiliko haya yanaathiri baadhi ya nchi na hata yetu inaweza kupata baadhi ya athari, lakini kwetu ni muhimu kuzingatia sera za nje kama ambavyo tumekubaliana,” amesema.
Majaliwa amesema: “Uwezo tunao, tunazo maliasili, tunazo rasilimali, kazi ambayo tunayo ni Watanzania kushirikiana kuhakikisha tunatumia maliasili na rasilimali tulizonazo kujenga uchumi wa ndani kuwezesha mipango na bajeti iweze kutekeleza haya.”
Amempongeza Rais Samia Suluhu Hassan, kwa kueendelea kuifanya Tanzania kuwa na mahusiano mazuri na nchi nyingi duniani ikiwamo Marekani.
“Sisi pamoja na upana wa mahusiano ambayo tumeyaweka ni kuhakikisha kwamba tunajiimarisha na kuwa na uwezo wa ndani. Lazima tujiimarishe kwenye mipango yetu, bajeti zetu ziweze kutekeleza maeneo yote muhimu ikiwemo sekta ya afya, elimu, maji na maeneo mengine kadri walivyokubaliana na nchi husika,” amesema.
Amesema kazi nyingine ni kuwezesha mipango na bajeti iweze kutekeleza yote.
“Niseme kuwa Marekani imeshatangaza na inawezekana na nchi nyingine zikatangaza kukawa na mabadiliko na sisi tunaendelea kujiimarisha kwa kuhakikisha kuwa tunakuza uchumi wetu kwa kutumia vyanzo vya fedha na mapato.
“Tunaweka pamoja na kuingiza hapa bungeni yapangiwe mpango kazi ili maeneo yaliyopungua tuweze kujaziliza, huo ndio mkakati sasa tunatakiwa kuwa nao na tunaweza kujipanga kutokana na mabadiliko ambayo sasa yanaendelea kwenye nchi zilizoendelea dhidi ya nchi zinazoendelea kama Tanzania,” amesema.
Bunge Februari 4, 2025 liliazimia Serikali itekeleze mpango wa kupata rasilimali za ndani kupambana na maambukizi ya Virusi vya Ukimwi (VVU) na Ukimwi bila kutegemea msaada wa wafadhili.
Azimio la Bunge lilifikiwa baada ya Mwenyekiti wa Kamati ya Kudumu ya Bunge ya Afya na Masuala ya Ukimwi, Elibariki Kingu kuwasilisha taarifa ya kamati hiyo kuhusu utekelezaji wa shughuli zake katika kipindi cha kati ya Februari 2024 hadi Februari 2025.
Kingu alisema kiwango kikubwa cha utekelezaji wa afua za VVU na Ukimwi nchini hutegemea fedha za wafadhili kutoka nje ya nchi.
“Ufadhili huo ukifikia ukomo unaweza kusababisha kwa kiasi kikubwa nchi kupunguza kasi ya kupambana na janga hilo kwa kukosa fedha za kutosha,” alisema.
a4465.en:
Summary:
- Prime Minister Kassim Majaliwa gives the Government's direction regarding United States foreign policy.

Dodoma. After the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) announced the suspension of funding, the Government has said it is strengthening itself to ensure it grows the economy by using [domestic] sources of funds and revenue to fill in the areas that have been reduced.

USAID announced the suspension of new funding and of disbursements under Development Objective Agreements (DOAGs) until the review of USAID-funded country assistance programmes is completed, within 85 days starting from January 24, 2025.

The review process aims to ensure that foreign aid is aligned with President Donald Trump's foreign policy agenda.

Prime Minister Kassim Majaliwa, answering an off-the-cuff question in Parliament today, February 6, 2025, said the Government is strengthening itself to grow the economy using the resources available so as to afford implementation in all the important areas, including the health, education and water sectors.

Majaliwa said this while answering a question from the Member of Parliament for Mbozi, George Mwanisongole, who asked how the Government is preparing to deal with the changes in United States foreign policy which are going to affect the implementation of Tanzania's policies in several areas, including education and health.

"How is the Government preparing for the changing policies of the United States, which, since President Donald Trump came to power, has made major changes to its foreign policy that are going to affect the implementation of our policies in education, health and the economy," he asked.

The MP named those projects as being USAID-funded: the Education Program for Results (EP4R) project and the programme to reduce the severity of HIV.

Majaliwa said Tanzania respects foreign affairs policies and implements the agreements of those policies as agreed with the countries concerned in various areas.

"We have begun to see countries with great capacity, including the United States, and these changes affect some countries, and even ours may suffer some effects, but for us it is important to observe foreign policies as we have agreed," he said.

Majaliwa said: "We have the capacity, we have natural resources, we have resources; the task we have is for Tanzanians to work together to ensure that we use the natural resources and resources we have to build the domestic economy so as to enable the plans and budgets to implement these things."

He congratulated President Samia Suluhu Hassan for continuing to make Tanzania maintain good relations with many countries in the world, including the United States.

"For us, along with the breadth of the relations we have established, the point is to ensure that we strengthen ourselves and have domestic capacity. We must strengthen ourselves in our plans; our budgets must be able to implement all the important areas, including the health, education and water sectors and other areas, in accordance with what has been agreed with the countries concerned," he said.

He said another task is to enable the plans and budgets to implement everything.

"Let me say that the United States has already announced, and it is possible that other countries may also announce that there will be changes, and we are continuing to strengthen ourselves by ensuring that we grow our economy using [our own] sources of funds and revenue.

"We put it together and bring it here to Parliament so that a work plan is drawn up so that we can fill in the areas that have been reduced; that is the strategy we now need to have, and we can organise ourselves in light of the changes now taking place in developed countries towards developing countries like Tanzania," he said.

On February 4, 2025, Parliament resolved that the Government should implement a plan to obtain domestic resources to fight HIV infection and AIDS without depending on donor aid.

Parliament's resolution was reached after the Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and AIDS Affairs, Elibariki Kingu, presented the committee's report on the implementation of its activities in the period from February 2024 to February 2025.

Kingu said that a large proportion of the implementation of HIV and AIDS interventions in the country depends on donor funds from outside the country.

"If that funding comes to an end, it could to a large extent cause the country to slow down the pace of fighting that scourge for lack of sufficient funds," he said.

The discovery followed a meticulous search of consolidated cargo flown in on Ethiopian Airlines from Bangkok via Addis Ababa.
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intensified its crackdown on drug trafficking networks across Nigeria, arresting a notorious drug kingpin, intercepting cocaine concealed in lipsticks, and destroying over 28,000 kilograms of cannabis in forest raids.
A statement released on Sunday by NDLEA spokesperson Femi Babafemi detailed a string of major operations conducted between July 7 and 12, 2025, targeting smuggling rings operating within and outside the country.
Cocaine and Loud Seized at Lagos Airport
At the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) in Lagos, NDLEA operatives intercepted parcels of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, concealed in microwave ovens imported from Thailand.
The discovery followed a meticulous search of consolidated cargo flown in on Ethiopian Airlines from Bangkok via Addis Ababa. The search uncovered 23 parcels of Loud weighing 11.3kg. A suspect, Ezenwegbu Chike, has been arrested in connection with the seizure.
In a related operation, the agency recovered 400 grams of cocaine concealed inside lipstick casings bound for Malabo, Equatorial Guinea. The illicit substance was hidden among cosmetic products and hair attachments at the airport's export shed. A businessman, Ezeikwelume Prince Afam, was apprehended on July 11 in connection with the smuggling attempt.
This bust followed an earlier interception of 420 grams of cocaine hidden in 84 lipstick tubes destined for the UK via a courier company in Lagos.
Year-Long Manhunt Ends With Arrest of Kingpin
In one of the most significant breakthroughs of the week, NDLEA’s Special Operations Unit arrested a long-wanted drug baron, Okechukwu Izugha, alias Okey Omeogo, at his wife's shop in Ijesha Market, Lagos, on July 9.
“Izugha came under NDLEA radar on 7th August 2024 after a 9kg cocaine was recovered from a suspect Obiora Joseph Agudosi, at a motor park in Orile, Lagos while going to deliver the consignment in the southeast. Izugha was identified as the owner of the seized drug,” the statement said.
Izugha had been on the run for nearly a year after being linked to a 9kg cocaine consignment seized from a courier in Orile, Lagos, on August 7, 2024.
During the agency's investigation into his network, Izugha’s wife, Maureen Izugha, was arrested on January 21, 2025, with 500 grams of cocaine at her beverage store. She was later convicted and sentenced to two years in prison. Unaware that the agency remained on his trail, Izugha resurfaced and was swiftly apprehended.
28,000kg of Skunk Destroyed in Edo Forest
In Edo State, NDLEA officers destroyed over 28,000kg of skunk cannabis grown on more than 11 hectares of farmland in Ewere Uzebba forest, Owan West Local Government Area. The operation, which took place on July 8, also yielded 82kg of processed cannabis.
The team came under armed attack from cartel members as they exited the forest. Although one operational vehicle was riddled with bullets, no injuries were reported, and the officers safely repelled the ambush.
Multi-State Raids Yield Massive Drug Seizures
Other major seizures recorded in the past week include 1,400 blocks of Ghana Loud (700kg) recovered at Okun-Ajah Beach; two suspects arrested along Ajah-Epe Expressway with 26kg of Ghana Loud, 123g of methamphetamine, 45g of Molly, and a delivery van, all in Lagos State.
In Borno State, Godwin Chimaobi Nwaobi was arrested with 18,759 ampoules of pentazocine, tramadol, and rohypnol. Another suspect, Abdulrahman Bello Ahmadu, was caught earlier with 10,000 pills of tramadol.
Also, 116,226 pills of tramadol and D5 were recovered from five suspects in raids at Gombe Main Market and along Gombe-Kano Road.
Sabiu Bala was arrested with 316.6kg of skunk along Okene-Lokoja expressway in Kogi State while Haladu Suleiman, 38, was arrested with 58.8kg of skunk in Gubuchi, Ikara LGA in Kaduna State.
In Taraba State, three suspects were caught at Lanka Viri checkpoint transporting 577,890 pills of opioids and 1.16kg of skunk hidden in a petrol tanker’s tyre compartment.
Three suspects were arrested with 48.1kg of skunk at Janguza Barracks area in Kano State.
